chore: Test `Optional<Struct>` garbage tag read on Swift Cxx-interop in release (#1320)

* test: repro Optional<Struct> garbage tag read on Swift Cxx-interop

Adds three runtime tests on TestObject that bracket an Optional<Struct>
round-trip bug on the Swift side of nitro's Cxx-interop bridge:

  tryOptionalStruct       Reuses the existing OptionalWrapper. An
                          Optional<{ optionalArrayBuffer?, optionalString? }>
                          round-trips cleanly. Establishes the lower bound.

  tryOptionalNestedStruct Adds OptionalNestedWrapper:
                            { count?, enabled?,
                              inner?: { start?: Side, end?: Side } }
                          where Side = 'left' | 'right'. An Optional<Struct>
                          with one 2-variant string-union enum reused
                          twice in the nested inner struct still
                          round-trips cleanly. Proves the bug is not
                          "any nested optional struct".

  tryOptionalEnumStruct   Adds OptionalEnumWrapper:
                            14 primitive optionals
                            + tier?: 'free' | 'pro' | 'enterprise'
                            + region?: 'us' | 'eu' | 'apac' | 'global'
                            + inner?: {
                                stage?: 'idle' | 'warmup' | 'active' | 'cool',
                                tone?: 'cool' | 'warm' | 'neutral'
                              }

                          Surface conditions:

                            iOS Debug    : passes
                            iOS Release  : fails with
                              "Cannot convert <Tier|Region|Stage|Tone>
                               to JS - invalid value: <garbage 4-byte int>"
                            Android      : passes on both TestObjectCpp
                                           and TestObjectSwiftKotlin
                                           (no Swift Cxx-interop in play)

                          The garbage value differs per call (observed
                          83886081 and 2003789939 in separate runs).
                          The Debug-passes / Release-fails split, paired
                          with non-deterministic garbage, points at
                          uninitialized padding bytes or an
                          optimizer-revealed layout mismatch in Swift's
                          Optional<Struct> projection across the
                          Cxx-interop bridge — not a stable
                          wrong-pointer or logic bug.

Together the three tests bracket the bug: small + few enums = works;
wide + multiple distinct string-union enum types under optimization =
corrupted enum tag.

Repro-only — no fix.

fix: Synchronize C++ `Promise<T>` state-inspection accessors (#1398)

* fix(core): synchronize C++ `Promise<T>` state-inspection accessors

`resolve()`/`reject()` write `_state` under `_mutex`, but `isPending`/
`isResolved`/`isRejected`/`getResult`/`getError` read it lock-free.
`JSIConverter<shared_ptr<Promise<T>>>::toJSI` runs those reads on the JS thread
the instant a hybrid method returns, racing an off-JS-thread `resolve()`
(`Promise::async` / `Promise.parallel` / a main-thread resolve). Data race on the
`std::variant _state`, flagged by ThreadSanitizer.

Make `_mutex` mutable and acquire it in the inspection accessors. The lock-free
bodies move to private overloads that take a `unique_lock` (the caller proves it
holds the lock), so `getResult()`/`isPending()`-style call sites stay intact
without recursive self-locking. `resolve`/`reject` set the state and drain the
listeners under a single lock via `takeResolvedListeners(lock)`/
`takeRejectedListeners(lock)`, then fire them outside the lock; the `NITRO_DEBUG`
state assert runs just before the lock. Same treatment for `Promise<void>`.

* refactor(core): address review feedback on Promise synchronization

- Remove takeResolvedListenersAndClearAllListeners / takeRejectedListenersAndClearAllListeners helpers; inline as std::move + clearAllListeners
- Restore readable if/else structure in addOnXxxListener, using lock.unlock() before invoking the callback instead of nested RAII blocks with early returns
- Capture result pointer inside the lock in resolve() to avoid a second lock acquisition

* refactor(core): drop listeners outside lock by moving instead of clearing

* Update packages/react-native-nitro-modules/cpp/core/Promise.hpp

fix: Compute `AHardwareBuffer` size in bytes, not pixels (#1445)

getHardwareBufferSize returned height * stride, but AHardwareBuffer_Desc.stride
is measured in pixels - so RGBA_8888 buffers were under-reported 4x. Any
ArrayBuffer wrapping a HardwareBuffer then exposed a 4x-too-small size, and
consumers copying into a correctly-sized pixel buffer overflowed the
under-sized allocation (OOB memcpy / SIGSEGV).

- Multiply height * stride by the format's bytes-per-pixel for the common
  packed RGB(A) formats.
- BLOB buffers: width is already the size in bytes.
- Unknown/planar formats (YUV etc.) keep the legacy value since their stride
  semantics are format-specific.

Also fix the NITRO_DEBUG size-equality check in copyHardwareBuffer: it read
the source buffer's size twice, making the check a tautology that could never
catch a mismatched destination.

fix: keep `| undefined` on array elements and Record values (#1478)

* fix(nitrogen): keep `| undefined` on array elements and Record values

`createType(...)` threads optionality through every nested position
except two: the array element type and the `Record<K, V>` value type,
which both hardcoded `isOptional = false`.

With `isOptional = false`, an element type such as `string | undefined`
falls into the union branch, which filters `undefined` out on the
assumption that it "is already handled as isOptional" — but for these
two positions it never was. The result is that `(string | undefined)[]`
silently generated `std::vector<std::string>` instead of
`std::vector<std::optional<std::string>>`.

Pass `isNullable()` for both, so a nested element is created exactly the
same way a parameter, tuple element or struct property of the same type
already is.

This makes `std::vector<std::optional<T>>` reachable for the first time,
which exposed a gap in the Kotlin JNI array bridge:
`KotlinCxxBridgedType.dereferenceToJObject(...)` switches on the type's
own kind, so an `optional` always took the `*ref` branch. For the five
kinds that require `.get()` (array-buffer, function, hybrid-object-base,
map, promise) an optional element generated `*__elementJni`, which does
not compile. `dereferenceToJObject(...)` now forwards to the wrapping
type for optionals.

Fixes #1202

* fix(nitrogen): Only treat `undefined` as optional in arrays & Records

`isNullable()` is true for both `T | null` and `T | undefined`, but in Nitro
`null` is a type of its own (`NullType`) and only `undefined` (or a `?`) makes
a type optional. Use the same `undefined`-only predicate that function returns
and Promise resolutions already used - extracted into `isOptionalType(...)` so
all four positions read the same - so `(T | null)[]` and `Record<K, V | null>`
keep their `variant<NullType, T>` shape instead of gaining an `optional<..>`
wrapper.

* test: Add Harness coverage for optional array & Record elements

`bounceOptionals(...)` only pinned the generated signature at compile time.
Running it asserts that `undefined` elements actually survive the round-trip
through C++, Swift and Kotlin - including a null `ArrayBuffer` array element
and a null `Record` value, which are the cases the JNI array bridge fix is
there for.

---------

Co-authored-by: Marc Rousavy <me@mrousavy.com>

test: Pin `null` vs `undefined` shapes in array & Record elements (#1514)

`bounceOptionals(...)` (#1478) covers `T | undefined` elements, which become
`std::optional<T>`. These pin the other half of the semantic: in Nitro `null`
is a type of its own, so it must stay a `variant<NullType, T>` and must never
turn into an `optional<..>`.

Arrays:
- `bounceNulls(...)`         - `(string | null)[]`
                               -> `std::vector<std::variant<NullType, std::string>>`
- `bounceOptionalNulls(...)` - `(string | null | undefined)[]`
                               -> `std::vector<std::optional<std::variant<NullType, std::string>>>`

Records, as separate methods so the map is actually returned and asserted
instead of only being converted into native and dropped:
- `bounceOptionalMap(...)`     - `Record<string, string | undefined>`
- `bounceNullMap(...)`         - `Record<string, string | null>`
- `bounceOptionalNullMap(...)` - `Record<string, string | null | undefined>`

`bounceOptionals(...)` loses its `map` parameter for the same reason - it is
covered by `bounceOptionalMap(...)` now, in both directions.

Each method is a compile-time shape assertion via the generated spec plus a
Harness test round-tripping `null`/`undefined` through C++, Swift and Kotlin.
They also guard the follow-up of narrowing the remaining `isNullable()` call
sites (parameters, tuple elements, struct properties), where `T | null` still
gains an `optional<..>` wrapper today.

fix: Mark react-native-nitro-modules peer dependency as optional (#1516)

Semver ranges never match pre-releases, so a required peer of "*" does
not match e.g. 0.37.0-beta.0. Package managers then install a second,
stable copy of Nitro next to the pre-release, and the native/JS version
guard throws "Nitro was installed twice" at runtime.

Marking the peer optional stops the package manager from resolving Nitro
on the library's behalf, leaving the app in full control of the version.

fix: Rename `CachedProp` to `ReactProp`, re-add legacy `CachedProp` as deprecated (#1517)

The v0.37.0 View props rewrite changed `CachedProp<T>`'s API (immutable
shared entry, `get()`/`isProvided()`/`hasSameValue()`), which broke
modules whose specs were generated by nitrogen <= 0.36.x - their generated
code uses the old mutable API (`.value`, `.isDirty`, 3-arg
`fromRawValue(runtime, value, oldProp)`) and no longer compiled against
the new core.

- Rename the new implementation to `ReactProp<T>` (cpp/views/ReactProp.hpp),
  and fold its now-single-use private helpers into `fromRawValue`
- Re-add `CachedProp<T>` exactly as it shipped in v0.36.5, marked
  [[deprecated]], so old generated specs compile again (with a warning)
- Update nitrogen to emit `ReactProp` and re-generate nitro-test specs
